correctness.rationale: At each world w, the predicate S(P)=some E_i[w] subset of P is a monotone truth-preserving disjunction of principal filters. It preserves binary intersections (hence normal distribution over all valuations) iff the finite cell family has a least member, necessarily the intersection R[w], so S equals the S5 box for R and nested formulas agree. Fixing R as a t-block partition, each E_i is a partition of the t labelled blocks. Normality means every quotient point is singleton in at least one agent partition, whose exact inclusion-exclusion count is H_r(t)=sum_j(-1)^j C(t,j) (sum_k(-1)^k C(j,k)B_{t-k})^r. The coverage condition forces common refinement exactly R; Stirling transform gives L_{n,r}. Fresh independent Python enumeration of all ordered r=2,3 partition tuples n<=5, including 140,608 cases at n=5,r=3, exactly reproduced 1,8,89,1449,31468; the formula gives 864347 at n=6. For r_n B_{n-1}/B_n−log n→c, factorial moments of uncovered singleton-cell count converge to e^(−kc), since a_{n,k}=1−ks_n+O_k(s_n²) and r_ns_n²→0. The chance R is not discrete is bounded by C(n,2)s_n^{r_n}→0, so the global normality probability converges to exp(−exp(−c)). The Poisson limit is analytic, not certified by finite checks.
residual_risks: The Poisson statement is for growing r_n uniform independent random partitions; not for fixed r or nonuniform laws.
The finite n<=5 census corroborates rather than proves the unrestricted formula.
